description:
The sql_compat capability engine has largely replaced ddl.py's dialect if/elif
chains (type dispatch is now table-driven via get_type_mapping(), down from ~13
branches to ~2). But residual literal-dialect policy remains inside DDL RENDERING
functions:
  - ddl.py:296  if dialect.lower() not in ("snowflake", "bigquery")  (map column)
  - ddl.py:351  if pk_columns and dialect.lower() not in ("clickhouse", "doris")
  - ddl.py:390  if dialect.lower() == "bigquery" / elif "clickhouse"  (view syntax)
These hardcode dialect names in the rendering path rather than resolving through a
capability table. They are the residual tail of the sql_compat migration.

Move this policy into the existing sql_compat capability predicates/data
(supports_complex_types, supports_foreign_keys, supports_views already exist) so
the DDL rendering functions carry no literal dialect names.

anti_patterns.dont: enforce a module-wide grep->0 ratchet that would forbid legitimate capability-table dialect keys.
re-add dialect if/elif to the rendering functions
anti_patterns.why: the whole point is to retire them into capability data.

preserves.behavior: Rendered DDL is byte-identical for every currently-supported dialect (snapshot before/after).
sql_compat capability semantics are reused/extended, not duplicated.

prior_art.concept: {'ref': 'benchbox/core/metadata_primitives/ddl.py:173', 'note': 'get_type_mapping() - the data-driven pattern the residual branches should follow.'}

{'ref': 'benchbox/core/metadata_primitives/ddl.py:522, :535, :550', 'note': 'supports_complex_types / supports_views / supports_foreign_keys predicates - extend these (or the sql_compat table behind them) to cover map-column, PK, and view-syntax policy.'}

{'ref': 'benchbox/sql_compat/ (registry.py, decision.py, resolver.py, inventory.py)', 'note': 'The capability engine that owns dialect-specific data; add the map/PK/view-syntax policy here, do not re-add if/elif to ddl.py.'}

verifications.description: DDL unchanged per dialect; rendering carries no literal dialect policy
verifications.expected: rendered DDL byte-identical per dialect (snapshot); rendering-scoped no-literal-dialect test passes

work_units.notes:
Replace the three literal-dialect branches (ddl.py:296/351/390) with capability
lookups: map-column support, primary-key-clause support, and view-syntax
variant resolved from one sql_compat table/registry. Keep the rendered DDL
byte-identical for every current dialect (this is a refactor, not a behavior
change).
work_units.summary: Resolve map-column, PK, and view-syntax policy via capability data, not literal dialect names

work_units.notes:
Add a test scoped to the DDL RENDERING functions asserting they contain no
literal dialect-name policy (assert behavior via capability data and a snapshot
of rendered DDL per dialect). Do NOT use a blunt module-wide
grep 'dialect.lower()' -> 0 ratchet: capability-table internals may legitimately
reference dialect keys; the smell is literal dialect policy in the RENDERING
path, not anywhere in the module.
